final.memo:
Herbalife is a cash-generative global nutrition company currently caught in the crossfire of a highly publicized, crowded short-seller campaign [D01, D03, D05]. The market is mispricing the company as a terminal business, ignoring its consistent ability to generate robust cash flows and its superior operational efficiency compared to peers [D03, D04, D06].

With an operating margin of 16.3% in 2011, Herbalife significantly outperforms peers like Nu Skin (13.4%) and USANA (13.3%) [D06]. We believe that as the regulatory uncertainty clears, the stock should trade closer to its peers at a 13x multiple; applied to our 2015 EPS estimate of $5.00, this yields a target price of $65.00 [D04].

The market's extreme skepticism has created a technical dislocation rather than a fundamental break [D01, D04]. We anticipate that as the business continues to report strong results and the short position is forced to cover, the stock will experience a significant re-rating toward its intrinsic value [D01, D04, D07].

Our role is that of a supportive observer rather than an activist; the company is already acting in the best interest of shareholders through an aggressive share repurchase program [D01, D03, D07]. We expect management to maintain this capital allocation strategy while continuing to provide transparency to dispel unfounded regulatory fears [D01, D03, D05].

Risks remain centered on regulatory scrutiny, as a finding of an illegal business model would render the equity effectively worthless [D01, D05]. However, the current valuation of 9.88x P/E provides a significant margin of safety, and we view the $30.00 level as a hard floor supported by ongoing cash generation [D04].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common equity [D05, D07]. We will exit quickly if the regulatory thesis breaks or if management abruptly abandons its buyback program without operational cause [D01, D04].
